# Dedication

---

> There was a man served by kings, famous by the name of the illustrious Sahib Dayal <note>original: "Sahib Dayal"; a prominent 19th-century figure</note>, distinguished by the title "Gaj" <note>original: "Gajopapada"; likely referring to the title 'Raja' or a specific honorific</note>, who was a member of the Lord's assembly of great splendor <note>original: "prabhu-prabhūta-prabhā-sabhā"; referring to the Legislative Council</note>. || 1 ||
>
> His son, Vanshiddhara, was well-known and well-behaved, just as the famous Vanshidhara <note>an epithet for Lord Krishna, the "Flute-Bearer"</note> was born from Vasudeva in this world.
>
> His son is the moon among the stars of the virtuous, named Mahachandra, whose footstool is served by the lords of the people. || 2 ||
>
> This *Collection of Planetary Combinations* <term>Yogavali: a treatise on astrological combinations</term>, which is a portion of the *Bhrigu Samhita* <note>A vast, legendary collection of astrological charts attributed to the sage Bhrigu</note>, was given by him in the city of Mumbai for the purpose of printing, for the benefit of the world. || 3 ||
>
> It has now been printed in the printing house named Venkateshwar by the illustrious merchant Khemraj, who is truly devoted to the preservation of ancient texts. || 4 ||
>
> Many years have passed on this path, and great expenses in silver were incurred; with great difficulty, this *Lamp of Astrology* <term>Jyotih-Pradipika: a metaphorical title for the illuminating nature of the text</term> was obtained. || 5 ||

---

<margin>1. He was made a member of the Legislative Council of India by the Lord Governor-General in that assembly of great splendor.</margin>

<summary>This dedication page traces the lineage of the patron Mahachandra back to Sahib Dayal and credits the publisher Khemraj of the Venkateshwar Steam Press for the difficult task of printing this astrological work from the Bhrigu Samhita.</summary>
<keywords>Sahib Dayal, Vanshiddhara, Mahachandra, Bhrigu Samhita, Yogavali, Mumbai, Khemraj, Venkateshwar Steam Press, Legislative Council of India, astrology</keywords>

--- Page 18 ---
<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Yoga-Sagara (Ocean of Yoga), a treatise on astrological combinations. The text establishes a dialogue between the sages Bhrigu and Shukra.</meta>

-># The Ocean of Yoga<-

Salutations to the Lord Ganesha. Having bowed to Keshav <note>Vishnu</note>, Shambhu <note>Shiva</note>, Brahma, and the Leader of the Ganas <note>Ganesha</note>, and keeping the previous teachings in mind, this **Ocean of Yoga** <term>Yogasagara: literally 'Ocean of Unions,' a text detailing specific planetary combinations and their karmic results</term> is composed. || 1 ||

In the Treta Age, thirty-three hundred thousand years ago, the **Ocean of Yoga** came into existence. || 2 ||

**Bhrigu spoke:** In the age of the Vedas, whether by birth or by inquiry, one who understands the measure of planetary combinations <note>yogas</note> becomes the performer of all successful deeds. || 3 ||

In this first chapter, there are fifty planetary combinations in sequence. Through the measure of the planets <note>kheta</note> within them, one should understand the collection of one's merits. || 4 ||

**Now, the names of the Yogas:**
Manohara (Heart-stealing), Saumya (Gentle), Yatudhanya (Sorcerer), Bhishanaka (Terrifying), Jimuta (Cloud), Vijaya (Victory), Ananda (Bliss), Pingala (Tawny), Viphala (Fruitless), Sama (Even), || 5 || Mahodadhi (Great Ocean), Pishacha (Ghost), Damini (Lightning), Chakradamini (Wheel-lightning), Vagbhava (Source of Speech), Shrimukha (Fortunate Face), Krura (Cruel), Gaja (Elephant), Adbhutasagara (Ocean of Wonders), || 6 || Urdhvoddhrita (Raised Upward), Nipata (Falling), Vilasa (Luxury), Shakra (Indra), Mahisha (Buffalo), Devendra (Lord of Gods), Raja (King), Shula (Spear), Bhaskara (Sun), and the famous Vishruta, || 7 || Padmasta (Seated on a Lotus), Daruna (Dreadful), Chandra (Moon), Chatuh-Sagara (Four Oceans), Sagara (Ocean), Bhratruhari (Brother-stealer), Ripughata (Enemy-slayer), Chhatra (Parasol), Vajra (Thunderbolt), Jagatpati (Lord of the World), || 8 || Vainashika (Destructive), Kalapa (Ornament), Manasa (Mental), Anubhava (Experience), Shubha (Auspicious), Varjita (Excluded), Hutabhuk (Fire-eater), Vanya (Wild), Nanda (Joyful), and Jiva (Life), in due order. || 9 ||

Whatever deeds were done in the beginning, and whatever the planetary positions were, such will be the state of good or bad results produced by those very planets. || 10 ||

If Saturn is in its exaltation <note>original: "tunge"</note> in the sign of Sagittarius, and the Sun is joined with Mars in Aries, and if Venus, Jupiter, or Mercury are also joined, the person becomes honored by kings and very wealthy. Such a person is stout, a donor, rich, possessing excellent gold, and filled with many gems. He approaches kings in the evening, has many sons and servants, and enjoys a long, delightful life. || 11 ||

This combination arises because of deeds performed previously in the "House of Hari" <note>likely referring to a temple or a specific spiritual act dedicated to Vishnu</note>. Because of this, he attains happiness in this life, becoming wealthy and honored by royalty. || 12 ||

He is born endowed with sons, grandsons, and so on—of this there is no doubt. However, in old age, great sorrow will certainly come from those same sons and grandsons. || 13 || Because he did not complete the "House of Hari" in the past, he is thus troubled.

**Shukra spoke:** What is the prayer to be chanted? Whose worship should be done? What should be given in charity, and what is the medicine? || 14 ||

**Bhrigu spoke:** One should chant the seven-syllable mantra of Saturn, and the six-syllable mantra *Shrim Hrim*. After chanting each two thousand times, wealth should then be given. || 15 ||

Seven *tankas* of silver and the same of gold; a copper vessel weighing thirty *palas* filled with clarified butter <note>ghee</note>; a bull, a goat, land, and cows should be given to a Brahmin. || 16 || One should also arrange for the gift of land in one's own country with full faith. By the performance of these gifts, one becomes free from disease and happy.

<summary>This opening page of the Yogasagara introduces a list of fifty astrological combinations (yogas) and describes the specific karmic rewards and remedial rituals for a person born under a powerful alignment of Saturn, Mars, and the Sun.</summary>
<keywords>Yogasagara, Bhrigu, Shukra, astrology, planetary combinations, karma, mantras, charity, Saturn, Ganesha</keywords>

When Jupiter <note>Jiva</note> is in a harsh sign <note>a zodiac sign ruled by a malefic planet like Mars or Saturn</note>, and the lord of the fifth house <note>the house of children</note> is considered harsh; when the lord of the tenth house <note>career</note> and the lord of the ascendant <note>the self</note> are harsh and situated in harsh houses || 19 || and the lord is aspected by Mars or Saturn, then that combination is indeed the **Combination of Splendor** <note>Vibhava Yoga</note>. In a previous life, service was performed at ancient holy sites <note>tirthas</note> and to sages repeatedly. || 20 || By that merit, he shall have happiness, be wealthy, and honored by kings. He will be fair-complexioned, restless, a good speaker, virtuous, soft-spoken, and wise. || 21 || He will be a donor in many places and treat friends and enemies equally. A fast on Tuesday <note>the day of Mars</note> must be observed; this is stated as certain. || 28 || A Mars Yantra <note>Bhauma-yantra; a geometric talisman</note> should be worn on the side according to the rules. By this gift and treatment, offspring are certainly obtained. || 29 || The defect of children dying in infancy <note>mritavatsatva-dosha</note> is destroyed, and the young boy becomes long-lived. Therefore, the gift, worship, and the talisman <note>yantra</note> must be performed in truth. || 30 || Having heard this, everything should be done; one should not delay at all. The question was asked by Kavi and explained by Bhrigu. || 31 || Thus ends the result of the **Combination of Splendor**. || 2 ||

When the Moon is in the first, sixth, or eighth house, joined with or aspected by harsh planets; and when Jupiter and Mercury are in a harsh sign, while a benefic planet is in a center <note>kendra</note> or a trine <note>trikona</note> || 32 || under a "benefic combination" <note>Saumya-yoga</note>, in a previous life, an illicit union was made with the wife of a maternal uncle. He will be a miser, prone to anger, and a source of grief to his son, wife, and friends. || 34 ||

[The sage] spoke: In a bronze vessel weighing eleven <term>palas</term><note>A traditional unit of weight, approximately 40-50 grams</note>, a pentagonal mandala should be drawn. || 35 || A female form should be fashioned in the center using sandalwood and unbroken rice. In front of it, one should draw a thunderbolt symbol and recite the nine-syllable mantra of the Goddess Durga. || 36 ||

This gift must be given and the recitation performed without any doubt. || 38 || Then, a fine wood-apple fruit should be consecrated with the <term>Maya-mantra</term><note>The seed-syllable 'Hrim' associated with the illusory power of the universe</note>. During the proper season, a meal of milk-rice pudding should be offered three times. || 39 || By the ritual of this gift, a son is born—of this there is no doubt. After wearing it upon the head, one should perform the worship of the priests. || 43 || On Mondays, a single meal should be taken as a special observance. Through the ritual of these various gifts, O Lord of Creatures, one becomes free from disease. || 44 || On Tuesdays, a fast at night should be observed for the sake of obtaining a son, according to the rules. Thus was the question asked by the poet [Shukra] and explained by Bhrigu. || 45 ||

### The Result of the Combination of Metals and Grains

If the lord of the fourth or eighth house is a malefic planet or joined with malefics; or if the Sun is in the sixth or eighth house, or in an enemy's sign, and malefic planets are in malefic houses: (62) But if Jupiter is in a quadrant, a trine, exalted, or in its own house, then in the case of Bhishmaka <note>likely the name of the seeker or a specific astrological profile</note>, happiness and prosperity will arise without a doubt. (63) In a previous life, this person performed service at holy pilgrimage sites and repeatedly served the sages. They performed worship of the gods and showed devotion to the twice-born <term>Brahmins</term> in that birth. (64) Consequently, they are happy, a performer of good deeds, righteous, and possessed of many sons. They enjoy life with many women and are intelligent and discerning. (65) They are a generous giver at heart, wealthy, and a leader among the affluent. When thirty years have passed, great happiness will surely arise. (66) They will be a king or honored by kings, equal to Kubera <note>the god of wealth</note>. However, after the fortieth year, suffering will arise. (67) Pain arising from 'blood-wind' <note>likely a circulatory or rheumatic condition</note> and the influence of 'royal disease' will manifest. Diseases such as cough and asthma will occur repeatedly. (68) One moment there is health, and the next moment suffering; the person becomes emaciated. (69)

One should observe <note>the ritual requirements</note>. A vessel should be covered with a woolen cloth and green-colored rice grains. || 72 || Seated upon this, one should perform ten thousand recitations <term>Japa|the meditative repetition of a mantra</term>. One should perform the ritual of the seed-syllable of Padmanabha <note>Padmanabha is a form of the god Vishnu, meaning 'the one with the lotus in his navel'</note> according to the rules... || 73 ||

Wearing silken garments and following the previously mentioned method, a gift should then be made: sixteen pieces of gold. || 74 || Double that amount of silver should be given, along with clothes... a hundred. Four copper vessels, each weighing one <term>Karsha|a traditional unit of weight, approximately 12 grams</term>, should be filled with clarified butter <note>Ghee</note> and presented to the Brahmins. || 75 || Then, one should offer a vessel filled with wheat and rice grains, along with twenty copper vessels weighing twenty <term>Karshas</term> each. || 76 || Having made this gift, one should also provide a priestly fee <term>Dakshina</term>. Thus, one should perform various types of charity endowed with faith. || 77 ||

If Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, the Moon, Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon; original: "Shikhi"</note>, and Saturn are placed in the houses of pleasure, memory, or action <note>the 7th, 5th, and 10th houses</note>, and if cruel planets are in the house of wealth or the ascendant, this is known as the **Moon-Setting Combination** <term>Chandrasta Yoga: a configuration where the Moon's influence is 'extinguished' or weakened</term>. **216**

By the influence of this combination, a person is born with a short lifespan. However, if this child survives, he shall become as wealthy as Kubera <note>the god of riches</note>. **217**

Otherwise, there is no happiness, no sons, and the person becomes chronically ill. **Shukra asked:** "What charity should be given? Whose worship should be performed? What mantra should be chanted, and what is the medicine?" **218**

### The Results of the Manasa Yoga || 43 ||

When benefic planets are in three houses and malefic planets are also in three houses; or when benefics are in the second and third houses, or auspicious planets are in the sixth or twelfth: || 348 || Then the **Anubhava Yoga** <note>The "Yoga of Experience"</note> occurs. Until the sixteenth year, there is great distress, disease, and a weak, flickering mind. || 349 || There will be suffering from bile and wind <note>Pitta and Vata humors in Ayurvedic medicine</note> along with some phlegm. **Shuka said:** This anxiety arose in the past; by what means can it be destroyed?
**Bhrigu said:** In a previous life, he was a killer of animals, specifically the female mates of forest animals. || 353 || Due to those sins, he becomes diseased or suffers through the faults of his sons.
**Shuka said:** What chanting should be done? Whose worship? What charity and what medicine? || 354 ||
**Bhrigu said:** For the Lord of the <term>Chidra</term> <note>The 8th house of obstacles</note> or the Lord of the Son <note>5th house</note>, one should perform ten thousand recitations of the **Five-Seed Nine-Planet** mantra, especially afterward. || 355 || An image of the animal should be made of sandalwood in a copper vessel weighing seven <term>palas</term> <note>A traditional weight</note>. Then charity should be performed of six, eight, or twelve pieces of gold. || 356 || Twelve pieces of silver, cloth, eighty-four thousand <note>units of currency or grain</note>, a **Sriphala** <note>A wood-apple or coconut</note>, five gems, a cow, and a buffalo should be given. || 357 || This charity should be performed in the eighth or twelfth year; or in the twenty-fourth or twenty-second year, one should practice this giving. || 358 || By the power of this charity, the fruit of progeny is ordained. A man becomes well-endowed with sons and grandsons and is liberated from the [negative] yoga. || 359 || This question was asked by **Kavi** and explained by **Bhrigu**. || 360 ||

### The Results of the Anubhava Yoga || 44 ||

If the lord of the ascendant is associated with auspicious and gentle planets, or is situated in its own sign of exaltation or in a cardinal house <note>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, and if other auspicious planets are located in their own houses, or in the houses of fortune <note>9th house</note> or wealth <note>2nd house</note>, then this is known as the **Auspicious Yoga** (Shubha Yoga). A person born under this name will be highly honored among kings, or will himself become a preeminent king, a sole abode of happiness, or a royal minister. || 362 || <insert>Thus ends the description of the fruits of the Auspicious Yoga through another method.</insert>

If the lord of progeny <note>Santanesha: the planet ruling the 5th house</note> is in an enemy's sign, or in the houses of wealth, the heart, the eighth, or the fifth <note>2nd, 4th, 8th, or 5th houses</note>, or if a cruel planet <note>malefic</note> is the lord of the house of intellect <note>5th house</note> and is aspected by auspicious planets || 363 ||, or if Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> or Saturn is in the fifth house from the ascendant, then the **Vaijita Yoga** <note>literally "Conquered" or "Defeated" Yoga</note> is formed, which destroys previous foundations. || 364 ||

Even if such a person achieves success by residing at holy pilgrimage sites, they remain childless due to these sins. Progeny will not be born to them, or if they are born, they do not survive. || 365 || His wife may be dominant, or she may pass away while some other remains.

**Shukra** <note>the planet Venus, acting here as a student</note> **said:** What should be chanted? Whose worship should be performed? What charity should be given, and what is the medicine? || 366 ||

**Bhrigu** <note>the sage and teacher</note> **said:** One should take a copper vessel weighing half a *pala* <note>a traditional unit of weight</note> and fashion a nine-fold mandala <note>sacred diagram</note> within it. In the center, one should create the form of a banner using sandalwood paste. || 367 || Then, one should chant the seed-mantra <note>Bija-mantra: a one-syllable sound used in meditation</note> of Saturn and Mars five thousand times, and thereafter, give gifts in charity. || 368 ||

The gifts should include twelve loads of silver, twenty loads of gold, cloth measuring eight handfuls, and a cow accompanied by a copper vessel. || 369 || Then, a pure coconut should be consecrated with the Maya-mantra <note>the syllable 'Hrim'</note>. This should be given to the wife at the end of her menstrual cycle, and one should observe a fast on Tuesdays. || 370 || Then the wise person should give a gift of a tree that resembles a cow <note>likely a symbolic representation or a specific species like the Kalpavriksha</note>. By the power of this gift, progeny is certainly obtained. || 371 || If one does not perform this charity, then for three lifetimes, there will be the death of sons and one will certainly suffer from chronic diseases. || 372 || Having heard this, one should perform all duties without any delay. This question was asked by the Poet <note>Shukra</note> and explained by Bhrigu. || 373 || <insert>Thus ends the result of the Vaijita Yoga. || 46 ||</insert>

When auspicious planets are in the house of fortune <note>9th house</note>, or Mars is in its sign of exaltation, and cruel planets are in the houses of improvement <note>Upachaya: the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses</note>, then a specific Yoga is born. || 374 || By performing chanting in a sacred place and giving food repeatedly, one becomes wealthy and happy through the power of that merit. || 375 || Such a person is wealthy, honored, large-eyed, famous, and a doer of many deeds. However, separation from father and mother occurs at the age of eight. || 376 ||

### The Void Combination (Shunya Yoga)
If Saturn is in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>, or if he is in Virgo, or in the eighth house; and if Mars and Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note> are in the third house, this is the combination named "Shunya" <note>Shunya means "Void" or "Zero".</note>. || 382 || In this Void state, the intellect wanders; things remembered are forgotten in an instant. With a void-like gait and a void-like mind, the man becomes a perpetual servant. || 383 || In the thirtieth year, the twenty-sixth, or even the forty-fourth, his wealth vanishes entirely—of this there is no doubt. || 384 ||

**Shukra spoke:** What is the prayer to be chanted, who is to be worshipped, what gift should be given, and what is the medicine?
**Bhrigu spoke:** One should chant the seed-syllables <term>Bija-akshara: core sounds used in mantras to invoke specific planetary energies</term> of Mars, Rahu, Saturn, and Mercury. || 385 || One should perform three thousand recitations with great effort. After the giving of gifts, a fire sacrifice <note>Homa</note> should be performed with the five nectars <note>Panchamrita: a mixture of milk, curd, ghee, honey, and sugar.</note>. || 386 || A grand bull should be given, along with wheat and oil. Salt and rock-salt should be offered, a *prastha* measure of each. || 387 || Jaggery and clarified butter <note>Ghee</note> should be given to a Priest with devotion and effort. Also silver of six-fold value and gold of eight-fold value. || 388 || A cloth of eighteen hands length, along with a meal and a monetary offering <note>Dakshina</note>. A copper vessel filled with ghee should be given to the one performing the chants. || 389 ||

**The Karmic Cause:**
In a previous life, this person insulted a holy man and bought or sold sacred knowledge <note>The "selling of knowledge" was considered a spiritual sin in ancient India, as wisdom was meant to be shared freely or supported by voluntary patronage.</note>. In this birth, this result is surely produced. || 390 || By the power of this gift, the Void Combination is destroyed. Otherwise, in old age, he dies of a feverish delirium and infirmity. || 391 || When one does not perform these meritorious acts, this fault persists. The question was asked by the Poet and explained by Bhrigu. || 392 || Thus ends the Result of the Void Combination. || 48 ||

### The Blissful Combination (Ananda Yoga)

After fifty years, there is great happiness and great wealth. || 394 || He gains royal honor through the power of some past merit. The question was asked by the Poet and explained by Bhrigu. || 395 ||

### The Śrīpuṣṭa Yoga
When **Bhṛgu** <note>Venus</note> is in the Ascendant, and **Jupiter** is joined with **Venus**; while the **Moon** is in the 9th house <note>the house of Dharma</note> and **Saturn** is in the 11th house <note>the house of gains</note>, this is called **Śrīpuṣṭa Yoga** <note>The Yoga of Abundant Prosperity</note>. || 9 ||
For the first ten years, the person's life will be a mix of happiness and sorrow. Then, for four years, they will be honored by kings and very happy. || 10 ||
From the age of thirty-two, they will enjoy happiness, possessed of wealth, grain, and sons. In this "Great Yoga" spoken by **Bhṛgu**, the person is very happy in their old age. || 11 ||
Thus ends the result of **Śrīpuṣṭa Yoga**. || 1 ||

### The Kārmuka Yoga
When **Jupiter**, **Venus**, or **Mercury** are in the 1st or 2nd house and aspected by the **Moon**, or if they are in their own sign or a friend's sign in the 4th house <note>hibuka</note>, one is happy. || 12 ||

Then it is **Kārmuka Yoga** <note>The Bow Yoga</note>. The man will be devoid of happiness. In the early period he will be sickly, and in the <unclear>end</unclear> it brings sorrow. || 14 ||
There will be anxiety regarding children, and he becomes chronically ill. This is because in a previous life, a sinful thought was directed toward the daughter of a Brahmin. || 15 ||
There is no happiness from children; this I speak truly.

When Jupiter is situated in the house of an enemy, then in the <term>Shrivatsa Yoga</term><note>A 'Yoga' is a specific planetary alignment; Shrivatsa is an auspicious mark associated with Vishnu, signifying 'the favorite of Fortune'.</note>, happiness and wealth are born; of this, there is no doubt. || 131 || Because in a previous life, the person repeatedly performed service at holy pilgrimage sites, worshipped the gods, and showed devotion to the <term>Brahmins</term><note>The priestly or scholarly class.</note>, in this current birth: || 132 || He will be happy, a doer of good deeds, possessed of a livelihood, and have many sons. When Rahu is situated in the third house <note>original: "sahajastha"</note>, Saturn is in the sixth, Jupiter is in the twelfth, and malefic planets occupy the trines: || 150 || This combination is known as the **Mudgava Yoga**. One born under this will be without children and afflicted by disease. Happiness is only achieved through limited wealth; of this, there is no doubt. || 151 ||

One should perform two thousand recitations <note>the practice of "japa" or meditative repetition</note> of the five-syllable mantra of Narasimha <note>The half-man, half-lion avatar of Vishnu</note>. This should be done while seated upon a woolen cloth, following the previously mentioned rites. || 152 || Forty-six units of gold and four times that amount of silver should be offered. A copper vessel weighing eleven units <note>original: "rudra-palam"</note> and a cow with her calf, yielding milk, [should be prepared]. || 153 || This gift <note>dana</note> must be performed when the Moon is auspicious and on a favorable day. By following this gift-giving, one's sons and brothers shall live. || 154 || The question was asked by Kavi <note>Shukra</note> and explained by Bhrigu. || 155 ||

Thus ends the result of the <term>Udbhava Yoga</term> <note>The Yoga of Origin/Manifestation</note>. || 15 ||

When malefic planets are in the first, ninth, second, or tenth houses, or in the seventh or fifth; or if planets are in their debilitation in the second or first house, this combination is considered "Terrible" <note>Bhishana</note>. || 156 || In a previous life, a practitioner of austerities was slandered, or a virtuous woman was disgraced. To remedy this, one should give gifts to her husband and perform acts of repentance. || 157 || One might possess forests and grain, yet experience growth one moment and decay the next.

**Shukra spoke:**
What is the mantra to be chanted, who is to be worshiped, what is the gift to be given, and what is the medicine? || 158 ||

**Bhrigu spoke:**
One should chant the mantra of Saturn three thousand times and the mantra of Ketu <note>The descending lunar node</note> two thousand times. A copper vessel of eleven units should contain a diagram of the nine planets <note>navamandalam</note>. || 159 || Having purified one's hands and feet, and being wrapped in a woolen cloth, one should sit upon it and perform the recitation according to the rules. || 160 || At the end of the recitation, a gold plate and a silver plate should be given. Red garments and ritual tools should be presented to the learned priests <note>Brahmins</note>. || 161 || The question was asked by Kavi and explained by Bhrigu. || 162 ||

Thus ends the result of the <term>Bhishana Yoga</term> <note>The Terrible Combination</note>. || 16 ||

When Saturn is in the ninth house, and a malefic planet or the Moon is in the fifth; and the Sun is in the ninth house of another, this combination is named **Saura**. || 163 || In a previous life, a pregnant peahen <note>shikhandini</note> was killed in the forest. # 21
## The Lotus Combination (Pankaja Yoga)

When Mars and Saturn are situated in the signs of Venus <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, and the lords of the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses are in the ascendant, or if the lord of the eighth house is in a trine <note>the 1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, this is known as the **Pankaja Yoga** <note>literally "Lotus Combination"</note>. **1**

The person born under this will be devoted to visiting holy sites, <unclear>active</unclear> and talkative, with a divine body and gentle eyes. They will have sparse hair, be a sweet speaker, and possess a very beautiful forehead. **208** They will be wealthy, happy, a seeker of pleasures, respected by kings, and a great lord. They will possess elephants, horses, and wealth, and will be a provider for their own servants. **209**

However, some suffering is experienced when the time becomes harsh. Therefore, one should perform charities and chanting <term>Japa</term> <note>meditative repetition of a mantra</note> at intervals. **210** In the first, eleventh, sixth, second, eighth, or fifth months or years, sudden distress may arise. **211**

**Venus spoke:**
What is the chant? Whose worship should be done? What is the charity and what is the medicine?

**Bhrigu spoke:**
The seed-mantra should consist of three syllables for Mars and seven for Saturn. **212** In front of a Nine-Planet Mandala <note>a sacred geometric diagram</note>, one should perform two thousand recitations. One should place a child <note>likely a small metal figurine representing the practitioner</note> inside a vessel made of twenty-two *palas* <note>a traditional unit of weight</note> of copper. **213** After consecrating it with divine scents, a bath with scented water is prescribed. That vessel should be filled with clarified butter <note>ghee</note> and joined with the five gems. **214** One should give a gift of gold, eight strips of cloth, and a blanket made of red threads. By the power of this charity, fierce suffering is dissolved. Having written the Nine-Planet Yantra <note>mystical diagram</note> on birch bark with "Yakshakardama" <note>a fragrant paste of sandalwood, saffron, camphor, and musk</note>, **215** one should wear it on the neck or arm; then the defect of the Yoga will be destroyed. This question was asked by the Poet <note>Venus</note> and explained by Bhrigu. **216**

**Thus ends the result of the Pankaja Yoga.**

## The Fire Combination (Pavaka Yoga)

When malefic planets are in the houses of wealth <note>2nd</note>, dharma <note>9th</note>, or loss <note>12th</note>, and the lord of the ascendant is joined with a malefic, there is suffering for the father at the time of conception, or the occurrence of execution and imprisonment. **217** This combination is named **Pavaka** <note>literally "The Purifier" or "Fire"</note> and it brings great distress.

**Venus spoke:**
What is the chant? Whose worship should be done? What is the charity and what is the medicine? **218**

**Bhrigu spoke:**
One should chant the mantra of the lords of the sixth and eighth houses, the lord of wealth, and the malefic planets. One should perform two thousand recitations, standing with pure hands, feet, and mouth. **219** At the end of the session, a gift should be given: a beautiful bed, equipped with all furnishings, and a milch cow with her calf. **220** One should give gold, ten strips of cloth, a ring with six gems, and a divine blanket and clothes to a <unclear>learned</unclear> person. **221** By the power of this charity, anxiety and distress are destroyed. <insert>A</insert> childless person obtains a son, and one whose children have died will give birth to a living child. **222** If these are lacking, great distress follows; thus it was explained by Bhrigu. **223**

**Thus ends the result of the Pavaka Yoga.**

# Results of the Yogas

## 40. The Bhringarita Yoga
If malefic planets are in the second house, benefics are in other houses, and Jupiter, Venus, the Sun, and the Moon are in the angular houses <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, while Saturn is in the third or fifth house, then the **Bhringarita Yoga** <note>literally "The Bee-like" Yoga</note> is formed. || 357 ||

The man born under this will be handsome, restless, soft-bodied, and happy. However, he will undoubtedly face great anxiety regarding wealth and expenses. || 358 || In his old age, he will experience great happiness due to the influence of his past meritorious deeds.

**Shukra <note>the planet Venus, personified as a student</note> asked:**
What is the prayer to be chanted, who is to be worshipped, what is the charity to be given, and what is the medicine? || 359 ||

**Bhrigu <note>the sage and teacher</note> replied:**
One should chant the seed-syllables <note>Bija mantras</note> of Shiva and Durga. One should perform two thousand recitations, especially on the banks of a river. || 360 || Holding a conch shell and forming the *Yoni Mudra* <note>a ritual hand gesture representing the womb/source</note>, one should perform the chanting. Following the previously mentioned rites, one should then perform acts of charity. || 361 ||

One should diligently offer to the Goddess and the God:
* Four *Prasthas* <note>an ancient measure of volume, approx. 640 grams</note> of wheat.
* Seven *Prasthas* of sugar.
* Two and a half *Prasthas* of clarified butter (ghee).
* Half a plate of gold. || 362 ||
* A pair of divine garments.

The worship should be performed specifically according to the instructions of the Guru. || 363 || Bhrigu has declared that a lack of charity leads to great sorrow.
**Thus ends the result of the Bhringarita Yoga.**

## 41. The Padma Yoga
When Jupiter is in the sign of Saturn, Venus is in the sign of Jupiter, and Saturn is in the sign of Venus, and these are in the angular, second, or fourth houses || 364 ||—or if Venus, the Sun, or Jupiter are in their exalted or own signs—then through the **Padma Yoga** <note>The Lotus Yoga</note>, one becomes a truly great man. || 365 ||

Liberation <term>Mukti: release from the cycle of rebirth</term> will certainly occur in the seventh birth; of this there is no doubt. However, sudden sorrow may arise due to the influence of a previous life. || 366 ||

One should diligently chant the three seed-syllables of Achyuta <note>Vishnu</note>. Then, charity should be performed: seven plates of gold || 367 ||, a horse, a cow, and beautiful, high-value clothing. Along with all household items, a blanket with red threads should be given. || 368 || By the power of this gift, the person will remain prosperous throughout their life. This question was asked by the Poet <note>Shukra</note> and explained by Bhrigu. || 369 ||
**Thus ends the result of the Padma Yoga.**

Born under the **Brahma Yoga**, a man will surpass his father. || 371 || From his birth, his father's happiness will increase day by day. || 372 || However, before the <unclear>years</unclear> mentioned, he may later become unhappy.

### 48. The Vishwananda Yoga
When Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note> is in the third house, Saturn is in the sixth, eighth, or third, and Jupiter is in the twelfth house, or if the lord of the house of merit <note>the 9th house</note> is associated with malefics; || 429 ||
When the lords of cruel houses are joined together and malefic planets are in the angles <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the pillars of a horoscope</term>, the **Vishwananda Yoga** is formed, which brings about the "Joy of the Universe." || 430 ||
<margin>The Vishwananda Yoga</margin>
However, [under this specific configuration], there will be anxiety regarding progeny and the possibility of disease in the body. **Bhrigu** said: One should chant the seed-mantra <note>Bija-mantra</note> of Saturn five or three times. || 431 ||
One should perform five thousand recitations according to the previously mentioned rites. Then, one should offer sixteen measures of gold and fourteen of silver. || 432 ||
One should perform the gift of a cow along with its calf and a copper vessel. By the power of this gift, one obtains the wealth of sons. || 433 ||
Bhrigu has declared that in the absence of such charity, great misery ensues.
-> **Thus ends the result of the Vishwananda Yoga.** <-

### 49. The Mahananda Yoga
When a planet is in its exaltation in a trine, an angle, or the house of gains <note>the 11th house</note>, and malefics are in the fifth house while benefics are in the trines; || 434 ||
Or if [benefics] are in the fifth or ninth houses, that is called **Mahananda** (Great Bliss). One born under Mahananda becomes highly honored, wealthy, and happy. || 435 ||
He is always victorious everywhere and possesses the wealth of sons and grandsons. This question was asked by **Kavi** <note>another name for Shukra/Venus</note> and explained by **Bhrigu**. || 436 ||
-> **Thus ends the result of the Mahananda Yoga.** <-

### 50. The Gola Yoga
When benefics are in the second and third houses, and malefics are also in the second and third, this is to be known as **Gola Yoga**. It indicates a child-killing <note>infanticide or loss of children</note> committed in a past life. || 437 ||
Because of that, one is born poor and foolish due to this Gola Yoga. If benefics are in the angles or trines, then indeed he becomes happy and wealthy. || 438 ||
Otherwise, there is constant worry regarding sons or the occurrence of disease. || 439 ||
**Shukra** <note>the planet Venus, acting here as a student</note> asked: What is the chant, who is to be worshiped, what is the gift, and what is the medicine?
**Bhrigu** said: Take a copper vessel weighing one Pala <note>approx. 48 grams</note> and draw a nine-planet mandala <note>sacred diagram</note> in the center. || 440 ||
This should be done with sandalwood paste, and the chanting should be performed before it. One should chant the letters of the Rudra-mantra <note>prayers to Shiva</note> and other hymns. || 441 ||
One should have a thousand recitations performed and then give the gift.
### 51.
Eight and six <note>fourteen</note> measures of gold and double that of silver; sixty pieces of cloth are prescribed, and especially a cow with its calf. || 442 ||
One should perform the service of Rudra <note>Shiva</note> daily for one full year. Through this charity, everything [positive] is born; so Bhrigu has declared. || 443 ||
-> **Thus ends the result of the Gola Yoga.** <-

In the <term>Avarga-yoga</term> <note>A specific category of planetary combination</note>, one was born from the mouth <note>referring to the Brahmin caste, traditionally said to be born from the mouth of the cosmic being Purusha</note>. Near the sacred site of Kedara, he was well-versed in the sciences and the Vedas. || 1 ||
He performed many acts of charity, especially on holy festival days. However, at one time, this <term>Vipra</term> <note>A learned Brahmin</note> committed a terrible deed. || 2 ||
Out of greed, he misappropriated wealth intended for a Brahmin's sacrifice. That Brahmin, turning his face away in disappointment, returned to his own home. || 3 ||
After some time, that learned man passed away. Bound by that specific action <note>his karma</note>, he fell under the jurisdiction of Yama <note>The god of death and justice</note>. || 4 ||
He underwent various births in the mortal world again and again. Eventually, he attained a human birth once more due to the influence of some residual merit. || 5 ||
In his 1st, 3rd, 6th, 8th, 12th, 18th, 24th, 36th, 39th, and 46th years, he shall suffer great hardship. His maximum lifespan is measured at seventy years, O twice-born ones. || 6-7 ||

Near the Vampa forest, there lived a man born of the warrior class <note>original: "bahujo," literally 'born from the arms,' referring to the Kshatriya caste</note> who was very powerful. || 8 || Having given all his wealth to the Brahmins, he went to a mountain cave. There, he performed intense penance facing the sun. || 9 || There, due to the force of destiny, <margin>Indeed he</margin> a certain independent woman <note>original: "svairini," often implying a woman acting of her own will or a wanderer</note> arrived. Abandoning his penance, he became devoted to her, becoming engrossed in pleasures like eating and other addictions. || 10 || He died on the banks of the Ganges and then went to the city of Indra <note>the celestial realm of the gods</note>. Then, when his merit was exhausted, he returned to the mortal world. || 11 || <term>2, 6, 9, 13, 7, 21</term> <note>These numbers represent specific years in the person's life where difficulties occur.</note> In these years, there is suffering. The maximum lifespan is 81 years.

### Now, the Antariksha Yoga <note>The "Atmospheric" or "Intermediate" combination</note>

One born in the Antariksha Yoga was a ruler of the earth in a previous birth. Having been the lord of the Kikata region <note>an ancient name for the Magadha/Bihar region</note>, he was a powerful ruler who administered harsh punishments. || 12 || He was devoted to punishing his soldiers and his subjects. Having committed forbidden acts <note>original: "agamyagamanam," usually referring to prohibited sexual relations</note> and having eaten what should not be eaten, O Twice-born <note>a term for a Brahmin</note>, || 13 || he lived there for many years through various cycles. He died as a hero in battle and then went to the city of Indra. After a hundred births, O Brahmin, he has attained human form again. || 14 || In the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 18th years, and likewise in the 29th year, great suffering occurs. His maximum lifespan is measured at 68 years. || 16 || <term>1, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29</term>

By eating the remnants of their food <note>Prasada; food sanctified by being shared with holy people</term> continuously for one month, he abandoned his former ignorance and set his mind upon the company of the virtuous <term>Satsang</term>. Leaving his own country, he became intent on bathing in sacred waters. After wandering to various pilgrimage sites and dedicating himself to various vows, he died on holy ground and was reborn. He was born into the family of the "foot-born" <term>Padaja; a term for the Shudra or laboring class, according to the traditional Vedic social hierarchy</term> on the northern bank of the Saraswati river. He was wise, devoted to the worship of Vishnu, and dedicated to the vow of truth. Skilled in the path of righteousness, he eventually became detached from worldly life. Remembering his past, he was then born as a "arm-born" <term>Bahuja; a term for the Kshatriya or warrior/ruling class</term> on the banks of the Sabarmati. O Son, hear the truth of this, his third birth: he is now intent on all comforts and is a constant devotee of Shiva. He will face hardship in his 1st, 3rd, 4th, 8th, 13th, 18th, and 22nd years. His maximum lifespan is 77 years.

### 29. Now, the Configuration of the Lustful (Kamiyoga)

In a previous birth, there was a certain merchant <note>Vaishya</note> devoted to righteousness. O highly fortunate one, he lived in the city of Mathura in that past life. || 162 || He wandered daily for alms and lived upon what he received. He gave gifts there during festivals according to his means. || 163 || However, a sin was committed by him with a mind overcome by lust; he committed adultery with a woman of his own caste. || 164 || She became pregnant by him, and he caused an abortion through the use of potent herbs and surgical instruments <note>original: "chedanakaih"</note> due to the fear of public scandal, O twice-born. || 165 || She certainly died from the pain of that induced abortion. Consequently, O best of the twice-born, he reached the City of Yama <note>the realm of the God of Death/Judgment</note> along with his companion. || 166 || Having experienced the fruits of sin through suffering and passing through various wombs, he is now born as a man: not very tall, of dark complexion, handsome, and possessed of modest wealth. || 167 || He is engaged in trade, prone to anger, endowed with strength and intelligence, but restless. He has brothers, but lacks happiness from his father, and is fond of women. || 168 || Due to the sin of causing an abortion in the past, he is without a son here. His lifespan shall be seventy-five years, and his end shall come in a holy land <note>original: "tirtha-bhumau"</note>. || 169 ||

### 30. Now, the Kaveri Configuration (Kaveriyoga)

Previously, there was a prince of cruel deeds but great majesty. Though wealthy in grain and riches, he lived in the land of Vanga <note>modern-day Bengal</note> at that time. || 170 || He gave cows, land, horses, and gold to those who recited the scriptures. However, O Brahmin, by the force of destiny, his mind was corrupted by greed. || 171 || In a boundary dispute, he unrighteously seized the property of Brahmins. || 172 || With the help of a single Brahmin, he committed this most terrible deed. He died there in a battle over land, urged on by Time <note>Death</note>. || 173 || Now he is born as a ruler of land in a beautiful place in the Middle Country <note>Madhyadesha</note>. He is fair-skinned, a scholar, yet very fierce; he has many daughters and is virtuous and successful. || 174 || This wise man gives according to his capacity; he is very tall and stays with his kinsmen. He is devoted to justice, intelligent, of a bilious temperament <note>pittikah</note>, sweet-spoken, and compassionate. || 175 || He has many wives, is famous, and possesses servants and vehicles. In his twenty-eighth year, he will experience a small amount of happiness regarding a son. || 176 || Due to the sin of stealing the property of Brahmins <note>original: "brahmasva-harana"</note>, he appears destined to be without a son. When forty years have passed, O Brahmin, a slight danger of death will occur. || 177 || If atonement <note>original: "prayaschitta"</note> is performed, O Brahmin, he may live for seventy-eight years. || 178 ||

### 45. The Karede Yoga

### 46. The Kanaka Yoga

### 96. Now, the Chakahari Yoga <note>A specific astrological combination, likely referring to a "Vegetable-Eater" or "Simple-Liver" configuration</note>

In the city of Mathura <note>A sacred city in North India, famous as the birthplace of Krishna</note>, where many people reside, there lived a wealthy potter <term>Kulala: a member of the potter caste</term> who was the best among the twice-born in his conduct. **427**

Through his work as a potter, he earned a great deal of wealth. He was known by the name Karmachandra, and his wife was named Devaki. **428**

Dedicated to his potter's craft, he went about his business day after day. As time passed, he eventually reached old age. **429**

Upon reaching old age, he was afflicted by poverty. He took a loan of wealth from a goldsmith for his business dealings. **430**

### The Union of the 'Ta' Group

### Now, the Tanka Yoga <note>Tanka Yoga: A specific astrological combination; 'Tanka' can refer to a coin or a stone-cutter's chisel.</note>
In this birth, a woman is barren, though in her previous life she possessed children. She should go to Kashi <note>Modern-day Varanasi, the sacred city of Shiva</note> and worship Lord Shiva with great effort according to the prescribed rites. Through fasts, charities, and great meritorious acts with various displays of wealth; then, on the night of Shivaratri, she should offer garlands of lamps and flowers. At midnight, she should bathe in the middle of the Great River <note>The Ganges</note>. Standing upon a boat while reciting the hymns to Varuna <note>The Vedic deity of water and cosmic order</note>—O Priest <term>Vipra: a learned Brahmin</term>, whoever performs this will surely obtain progeny.

### Now, the Tankara Yoga <note>Tankara: Referring to a twanging sound, like that of a bowstring.</note>

Difficulties at years: 2, 4, 6, 9, 10, 15, 20. Maximum lifespan: 72 years.

### 8. Now, the *Ta-me* Combination
<note>original: "Atha Ta-me Yoga"</note>

Difficulties in the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 9th, 10th, 14th, 16th, 20th, 25th, 28th, and 30th years. The maximum lifespan is 67 years.

Difficulties in years: 1, 2, 8, 13, 18, 22, 26, 30. Maximum lifespan: 90 years.

# # 44 Now, the Tīkara Yoga

Fourteen <term>krosas</term><note>A krosa is an ancient Indian measure of distance, roughly equivalent to 2 miles or 3.2 kilometers.</note> from the beautiful city of Ayodhya, there lived a very powerful man of the <term>Shudra</term><note>The fourth social class in traditional Indian society, often associated with labor and service.</note> caste named Dambara. **229** His wife was Chitra, who was devoted to serving her husband. He was always engaged in serving his Guru and earned his living daily as a vegetable seller. **230** O Twice-born <note>original: "dvija"; a term for a member of the upper three castes, here addressing the reader/listener</note>, he kept a white female cat. When she became pregnant, he killed her. **231** After a long time, that Shudra died. Because he died near the holy celestial river <note>The Ganges</note>, he went to heaven. **232** After enjoying the fruits of heaven for sixty thousand years, he was reborn as a human, endowed with wealth and grain. Many daughters were born to him, but no son at all. **233**

Difficulties in years: 1 | 3 | 8 | 12 | 15 | 17 | 20 | 27 | 36. Maximum lifespan: 88 years.

# # 45 Now, the Torī Yoga

The city of Kashi <note>Modern-day Varanasi</note> is famous and worshipped by the gods in the three worlds. Fifteen krosas to the west of it, **234** in the beautiful town of Mandavya, many people lived. Among them lived a Shudra who was devoid of pride. **235** His excellent wife was named Dindima. He had accumulated wealth but had not given any in charity in the past. **236** Once, by a stroke of fate, Brahmins were invited. ### 49. The Tarana Yoga
In a previous life, a certain man lived in the land of Vanga <note>Modern-day Bengal</note> born into a family of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija"; referring to the upper three castes, likely a Brahmin here</note>. He was then born into various animal forms for many thousands of years. Finally, he attained a human birth due to some small remnant of merit. **[264]**
Hardship occurs in the 1st, 5th, 9th, 13th, 18th, 22nd, 26th, 32nd, and 36th years. Maximum lifespan: 105 years.

### 50. The Timakara Yoga

After many thousands of years, he has been born again as a human. **[269]**
Hardship in the 1st, 3rd, 7th, 12th, 15th, and 20th years. Maximum lifespan: 75 years.

Hardship in the 1st, 2nd, 5th, 7th, 10th, 16th, 20th, and 24th years. Maximum lifespan: 66 years.

### 2. The Tattva Yoga

# 61. The Yoga of the Mark
<note>original: "Lekha yoga"</note>

In a previous birth, there was a cowherd <note>original: "Abhira"</note> living in the <term>Antravedi</term><note>The fertile region between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers</note> region. A servant of good people, compassionate, a Brahmin who was an ocean of virtues—yet, he was a destroyer of all his good deeds because he constantly drank wine. || 32 ||
At one time, O Brahmin, the wife of his <term>Guru (teacher)</term> arrived. She was pulled by force, and he committed an act of lust upon her against her will. || 33 ||
Because of that very sin, he was born into the animal womb. He became a jackal, then a donkey, and also a pig. || 34 ||
He spent eighty thousand years in the Great Cauldron Hell <note>original: "Mahakataha-naraka"</note>. After that, he was born as a human with a terrifying and formidable appearance. || 36 ||

**Hardship in years:** 1, 3, 8, 12, 17, 21, 24, 30, 36.
**Maximum lifespan:** 105 years.

## 106 **Now, the Sanga Yoga ||**

Long ago in Kalinga <note>An ancient region on the east coast of India</note>, there was a Brahmin who was a seeker of the truth of knowledge. He was steadfast in the knowledge of the Absolute <term>Brahma-jnana</term>, but he had no inclination toward the path of devotion <term>Bhakti-marga</term>. || 450 || Once, a great devotee of Vishnu <term>Vaishnava</term> engaged this Brahmin in a debate on the meaning of the scriptures. Although the Brahmin was defeated, he did not embrace the path of devotion in his heart. || 451 || That devotee, having given up his body while on a pilgrimage to holy places and having enjoyed many pleasures in heaven, has now come to the earth...

<margin>1.7</margin> **Now, the Sangavalin Yoga.** <note>original: "Sangavalin-yoga"</note>
Those born under the Sangavalin Yoga lived previously in the Chola country <note>A historical region in Southern India</note>. He was a merchant <term>Vaishya: the merchant and agriculturist class</term>, exceedingly compassionate, and endowed with all good fortune. || 464 || Once, a guest arrived at his home, but he did not offer any alms. Due to that sin, after dying and suffering misery in the abode of Yama <note>The God of Death and Justice</note>, || 465 || he returned to the surface of the earth and became poor. Though having a family, he is greatly distressed; he may find happiness through the worship of the gods. || 466 || There will be hardship in the 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 20th years. The maximum lifespan is 65 years.

<margin>1.8</margin> **Now, the Shauri Yoga.**
One born in the Shauri Yoga was previously a Kshatriya <note>original: "Bahuja," meaning born from the arms (of Purusha), a synonym for the warrior caste</note>. Having ruled his kingdom righteously, he once committed a sin. || 467 || By having a forbidden relationship within his own lineage <note>original: "sagotra-ramanam," implying incest or violation of clan exogamy</note> and gaining a bad reputation in the world, he died and was taken by the messengers of death to the realm of Yama, O best of the twice-born. || 468 || Having suffered the fruit of his sin there, he has come to the surface of the earth. Because of that past, he is always afflicted by chronic disease. || 469 || Peace may be achieved by sponsoring the marriage of a Brahmin’s daughter, and not otherwise. || 470 || Hardship in the 1st, 26th, and 30th years. The maximum lifespan is 80 years.

<margin>1.9</margin> **Now, the Sobhani Yoga.**
One born in the Sobhani Yoga was a fisherman in a previous birth. Even after killing many fish, upon dying, he went to the abode of Yama. || 471 || Having suffered the fruit of his sin there, he has come to the surface of the earth. Due to the remnants of that sin, his sons shall perish. || 472 || O best of the twice-born, one should have the name of Rama written one hundred thousand times, accompanied by the proper verses. One should also offer balls of dough to the fish. || 473 || Then there shall be happiness regarding progeny, and not otherwise, O best of the twice-born. || 474 || Hardship in the 3rd, 7th, 10th, and 16th years. The maximum lifespan is 75 years.

<margin>1.10</margin> **Now, the Sharanagata Yoga.** <note>The "Yoga of the Refugee" or "One who seeks shelter"</note>
In the beautiful city of Purushottama, there lived a man with his family. He possessed incomparable wealth and power, and was known by the name Devalo. He was a Shudra <note>original: "Padaja," meaning born from the feet, referring to the laborer class</note>, a speaker of truth, honored in assemblies, and wise. || 475 || At one time, O sinless one, with a mind greedy for a Brahmin's wealth, he spoke a lie before the King for his own sake. || 476 || Because of that sin, <unclear>he resided in the realm of Yama</unclear>. He then became a monkey on the banks of the Gomati river before becoming a human again. || 477 || In this birth, he has become wealthy and possessed of grain. For the sake of a son...

## An Appeal to the Learned.

At our printing house, the following works are available for purchase at reasonable prices, beautifully printed with the finest soft-lead type <note>referring to high-quality movable metal type used in the late 19th century</note>: the Rigveda and other Vedas; the Upanishads; works on Vedanta; historical epics such as the Mahabharata; the Great Puranas and secondary Puranas including the Shrimad Bhagavatam; and scholarly treatises on Sacred Law <term>Dharmashastra: codes of conduct and law</term>, Ritual Manuals <term>Karmakanda</term>, Grammar, Logic, Yoga, Samkhya philosophy, and Hermeneutics. We also offer literature such as Poetry, Drama, and Mixed Prose-Verse <term>Champu</term>, as well as numerous hymnal collections like the Thousand Names <note>Sahasranama</note> and various books in different languages.
